text:
anya: FYI — bringing up Nereid 14b (int4) canary. Seeing OOMs on warm starts when max_new_tokens >= 1024, then memory fragmentation spikes and stays high. attaching short logs.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed for nereid14b-int4 on pool-gamma. 12 instances.
leo: thanks. repro steps? env + payload size?
anya: repro is simple: single-stream chat with long generation (>=1200 tokens). reproduces on both microbatch=1 and microbatch=2 on some GPUs.
ciara: suspect KV cache slot fragmentation + allocator churn. we've seen similar with other 14b on int4. try enforcing early KV eviction and prefetch=false for warm starts.
ben: log snippet — OOM point:
```
[OOM] cudaMalloc failed: OutOfMemory
allocating 1.2GiB for attn_kv
post-oom: free list fragmentation: free_chunks=14, largest=64MiB
```
leo: can we try lowering default max_new_tokens for this model to 512 and enable slab compaction on evict? small change but often helps.
anya: +1 to lowering default. also propose short warmup run that primes KV caches (100 token dummy request) before accepting production traffic.
ciara: microbatching tweak: keep batch_size=1 for latency, but allow max_concurrent 2 for bursts and add small batching window (20ms). reduces per-token alloc churn.
ben: i'll run an overnight A/B: current default vs new defaults (max_new=512, prefetch=false, kv_eviction_threshold=0.6, slab_compact_on_eviction=true). command:
```
./canary_runner --model nereid14b --quant int4 \
  --max_new_tokens 512 --prefetch false \
  --kv_eviction_thresh 0.6 --slab_compact true \
  --workload long-gen --duration 8h
```
leo: also collect alloc histograms and large-free-chunk counts every 5m so we can chart fragmentation over time.
anya: add quality eval too — run 1k prompts from conv-bench and compute Rouge/LLMScore to ensure quant+defaults don't regress.
ciara: if A/B looks good, plan for rollout: canary -> 30% (24h) -> 60% (24h) -> full. include auto-fallback to fp16 variant if OOM rate > 0.5%.
ben: ack. starting run now. will post results tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
leo: thanks all. if we still see tail OOMs we'll try kernel affinity + small page-alignment patch next.
anya: noted. tagging infra to reserve a few spare nodes in case we need live debug (ping @leo for allocation).
